ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Raising the eyebrows and blinking is an observable facial response whose value changes with the encounter; the action itself does not certify what it means.
EvidenceBody: Mazu Daoyi explicitly makes the gesture right at some times and wrong at others. A questioner says it is not yet an adept’s working, while Zhongji Kezun and Dongshan Shouchu compare formulaic gesture to confinement or a kitchen rag.
A visiting monk reports it as evidence of pervasive awareness; Tianran Hanshi analyzes Mazu’s alternating use, and Chushi Fanqi condemns instant certification based on the gesture alone.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: A minute facial action becomes a public test of timing and discrimination precisely because the same motion can be accepted, denied, copied, or over-read.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The corpus supplies no stable inner state readable from the gesture; Mazu’s fourfold statement and Chushi’s criticism forbid treating it as automatic proof.
